_comment_what: THE single pin for the @talchain/schemas contract artifact used by the ISL drift check (tests/contract_drift/). The committed artifact talchain-schemas.json in this directory MUST be byte-identical to what scripts/contract_schema/refresh_contract_schema.sh regenerates from this pin — CI's contract-drift freshness gate enforces that. Change the contract snapshot ONLY by editing this file and running the refresh script; hand-editing talchain-schemas.json is exactly the hand-maintained-mirror defect this check exists to kill.
_comment_upstream: The artifact is GENERATED locally from the schemas repo at the pinned ref below by scripts/contract_schema/generate_contract_schema.mjs. (History: this was originally a fallback because the intended JSON-Schema export on olumi-schemas branch 'a3-json-schema-publish' did not exist on the remote when the check was built, verified 2026-07-20 by git ls-remote. That branch still publishes no artifact, so local generation remains the mechanism — it is now the sanctioned path, not a stopgap. If a published JSON-Schema artifact ever ships, switch the refresh script to fetch it instead of generating.) 'ref' is now a RELEASE TAG rather than a raw main-tip commit, as the original note directed. A tag is safe to pin here even though tags are mutable in principle: the freshness gate re-derives from the ref and FAILS LOUD on any byte difference, so a moved tag surfaces as a red gate rather than a silent snapshot change. The resolved commit is recorded in ref_kind for immutable evidence.
_comment_bump_2160: Bumped 0.20.0 -> 0.30.0 for ROADMAP 2.160 (contract alignment, 2026-07-30). The reason for THIS bump: the four VOI keys — correlation_model, decision_evpi, factor_evppi, p_win_sensitivity — were carried in drift_baseline.json as ACCEPTED-SUPERSET exceptions ('ISL emits ahead of contract adoption'). Contract 0.30.0 ADOPTS all four on boundary.AnalysisEnrichmentSchema, which is exactly the schema ISLResponseV2 is paired with (drift_core.PAIRINGS). An exception for an adopted field is a hand-maintained mirror that HIDES real drift: while a key sits in the superset baseline the check never compares ISL's emitted domain against the contract's declared domain for it, so a genuine type divergence stays invisible. The four entries are therefore REMOVED — and removed by re-deriving the baseline, never by hand.
_comment_bump_2798: Bumped 0.30.0 -> 0.38.0 for ROADMAP 2.798 (2026-08-07). The reason for THIS bump: ISL declared `GoalConstraint.value_frame: Optional[Literal['level','delta']]` (src/models/robustness_v2.py) as the READER half of value_frame adoption, describing itself as mirroring `@talchain/schemas` 0.38.0 `DraftGoalConstraint.value_frame` — while this pin still sat at 0.30.0, which does not carry the field at all (measured: 0 occurrences of `value_frame` in the 0.30.0 artifact). ISL's Python model was therefore AHEAD of its own contract pin with nothing policing the divergence: the freshness gate re-derived from a contract that knew nothing about the field and passed 2.798 without ever comparing name, enum domain or optionality against the TS source of truth. That is the hand-maintained mirror this whole directory exists to kill. TWO changes were needed, and the pin bump alone is NOT sufficient — see _comment_pairing_2798.
_comment_pairing_2798: WHY THE PIN BUMP ALONE WOULD HAVE BEEN THEATRE. Bumping the pin puts `value_frame` into the artifact (0 -> 5 occurrences, `boundary.DraftGoalConstraintSchema` among them) but the drift check only compares models listed in drift_core.PAIRINGS, and `GoalConstraint` was in NO pairing — it is a REQUEST model, while PAIRINGS covered only the compute-seam RESPONSE family. So a fresher artifact would have carried the field past a check that never looked at it: the field would sit in the fixture, unread, and every later session would see a green gate and believe the mirror was policed. `GoalConstraint -> boundary.DraftGoalConstraintSchema` was therefore added to PAIRINGS in the same change, which is what makes the domain comparison actually run (ISL `null/string {delta, level}` vs contract `string {delta, level}` — accepted). Measured effect of the pairing: +6 OPTIONAL omissions (confidence, deadline_metadata, provenance, provenance_unit_normalised, source_quote, unit — contract-side fields ISL does not consume), 0 supersets, 0 new collisions, 0 new REQUIRED omissions.
_comment_bump_2798_other_drift: OTHER DRIFT SURFACED BY THE EIGHT MINORS (0.30.0 -> 0.38.0), measured before landing: 183 -> 193 contract exports; NO new collisions (22 before, 22 after — the fail-loud class is unchanged); omissions unchanged at 44; and exactly ONE superset exception DISSOLVES — `OutcomeDistributionV2.percentiles_source`, which 0.38.0 adopts on boundary.EnrichmentOutcomeStatsSchema. That is the same pattern as the VOI family at the 0.20.0 -> 0.30.0 bump recorded above, and it matters for the same reason: while an ISL-emitted key sits in the superset baseline the check NEVER compares ISL's emitted domain against the contract's declared domain for it, so the exception must be removed by RE-DERIVING the baseline (scripts/contract_schema/refresh_drift_baseline.py --refresh-baseline), never by hand. Paired-schema property changes across the bump: AnalysisEnrichmentSchema (critiques, flip_thresholds, option_comparison), EnrichmentOptionComparisonEntrySchema (outcome), EnrichmentOutcomeStatsSchema (+percentiles_source).
